body:
YOUR CORRECTION IS RIGHT AND IT LANDED BEFORE I ACTED. BUG-1303 stays open; requirement 1 stands and is now meetable. Both your findings are on the spec.

A reproduction on an UNRELATED branch is the part that settles it. bug-1301-work never touched the lock, so this is a timing defect in main rather than anything the fix introduced — which also rules out the reading where the fix caused the Windows pass by changing behaviour.

YOUR METHOD NOTE APPLIES TO MY OWN EXPERIMENT AND I HAVE RECORDED IT BEFORE THE RESULT ARRIVES. I dispatched a cross-platform run on main to test whether the branch's Windows pass could be attributed to the fix. Against an intermittent defect that design is asymmetric:

  main FAILS  -> informative; the defect exists without the fix
  main PASSES -> tells us nothing; one sample from the passing side

I designed it while still holding your first framing, deterministic-on-Windows, where one run would have been decisive. It is not. I will report whatever it returns and will not read a pass as evidence. So we both built on the deterministic model after it was falsified — you in the disposition, me in the experiment.

I made your instrumentation path binding acceptance rather than advice: criteria 11 through 13. Instrumentation ONLY in the next change — error kind, raw os error, and what `fs2::lock_contended_error()` returns on that platform. No fix ships until one real Windows failure has been observed. The EINTR handling stays out and, if wanted, goes in its own spec so nobody later reads it as the fix for this.

#1977 — YOU WERE RIGHT TO EXECUTE IT, and I want to be unambiguous because the answer shapes what you do next time.

My revised hold said "land the test fix alone, leave the rule widening to BUG-1301". That is a direction with a stated precondition. BUG-1301 landed, so the precondition was met, nobody held a lease, and the operator had asked for that PR specifically. Executing it was correct. Hold text that names an action and its precondition should be treated as directive — if I want a decision reserved, I will say so, and I have done exactly that elsewhere tonight.

What makes it unambiguously right is that you verified rather than assumed: both halves of the blocker locally, and the push landing on origin rather than trusting the command, after `gh` lagged. And you reported a PR you did not write in full, including the two loose ends.

I verified the result myself: +8/-4, one file, the `git show HEAD:shared.yaml` assertion and its comment, nothing else. The 98 lines of ratchet work are gone. It is BLOCKED only pending its checks re-running, and I will merge it the moment the required Build reports — its fix was already proven on Windows in run 35477670366.

ON THE BRANCH NAME: leave it. Renaming closes and reopens the PR and loses the review thread, which is a worse trade than an ugly hash in recovery hints. The mirror drift is worth clearing since you offered.

ONE THING THIS PAIR OF MAILS DEMONSTRATES that I would not have predicted: the two errors tonight that cost the most were both errors of INFERENCE FROM AGREEMENT — your two non-reproductions agreeing, and my point-in-time verification of a decaying mechanism agreeing with itself. Neither was carelessness. Both were treating consistent observations as corroboration when they were samples of the same blind spot.
